baer-heitev/5:ב: When it darkens. Magen Avraham wrote: but on the night of the second Yom Tov he is obligated in all mitzvot — specifically on the second day Rosh wrote that Chazal made it like weekday; but on the night before it, no; all the more for us who practice burial needs through a gentile — he is obligated at night; so too Maharil: where one died on erev Shabbat — permitted to sanctify on Shabbat night; but by day all agree he is exempt; only he should not recite the Haggadah on Pesach since it contains midrash on verses — Mordechai is troubled; so too in Darkei Moshe Yoreh De'ah siman 341; Taz disagrees with Shelah there — see there; it implies by day even if he does not wish to bury now, aninut applies, for Chazal made it like weekday; nevertheless it appears to me if impossible to bury due to gentile danger or other coercion, aninut does not apply. It implies from responsum Mordechai that forbidden to read Torah until here his words — see there:
baer-heitev/8:_: Before. One whose father or mother died and completed per the second view day-for-day the first festival day and they rebuked him during the festival — permitted to shave on chol hamoed, since he could not shave on erev Yom Tov. Leket Yosher part 1 siman 285:
baer-heitev/10:ב: Prohibition, etc. — meaning by law; but the custom is to be lenient as Rama wrote Yoreh De'ah siman 399 seif 5. Shach, Taz, Bach, and later authorities; Peri Megadim:
baer-heitev/19:_: On Shabbat. Taz wrote [Yoreh De'ah siman 402 seif 6 I wrote]: if one died on Shabbat and the seventh day is Shabbat — one does not practice prohibition in private matters except in the morning at sunrise; therefore permitted at Mincha to read him from a Torah scroll; I further wrote there: if the seventh day is Shabbat they practice somewhat in households to sit on the ground at night one hour — it is a gross error unless one heard a distant report on Shabbat, then they practice aninut one hour at night; not like Bach Yoreh De'ah siman 402 s.k. 4 as I wrote:
magen-avraham/3:א: Died on Yom Tov — specifically seven mitzvah dead; see Yoreh De'ah siman 399 b'dieved:
magen-avraham/10:ד: And for us, etc. — meaning by law; but custom to be lenient as Rama Yoreh De'ah 399:5 [Shach, Taz, Bach]; Tashbetz siman 287 wrote: one who died on erev Shabbat and that Shabbat is erev the festival — permitted to wash in hot water on erev Shabbat — see there; requires study, for siman 426 implies they permitted only because of obligatory immersion — implying on other festivals forbidden; therefore it appears what Rama wrote in Yoreh De'ah and "so they practice" refers to those who do not practice bathing prohibition all thirty days; but for us Rama holds bathing prohibition on other festivals, only on Yom Kippur permitted; nevertheless it appears to be lenient since all later authorities are lenient:
mishnah-berurah/3:ג: (12) Day of death and burial — but if he died yesterday and was buried on the last day, the burial day is from Torah and does not override Yom Tov even though it is only rabbinic:
mishnah-berurah/10:ה: (39) Some permit bathing, etc. — specifically bathing; but other mourning laws such as sitting on the ground and removing shoes apply until dark [Magen Avraham]:
mishnah-berurah/10:ח: (42) For the festival is not nullified, etc. — nevertheless custom is lenient as Rama Yoreh De'ah 399:5; some later authorities hold one should not be lenient for hot bathing only cold [nevertheless on chol hamoed certainly rely to be lenient]; even per the lenient, hot bathing is only on erev Yom Tov and on chol hamoed because of festival honor; but after the festival bathing and laundering forbidden until thirty, for the festival did not nullify the thirty-day decree; see Hagahot Imrei Baruch Yoreh De'ah 399:
mishnah-berurah/14:_: (44) Who shaves on Yom Kippur — for it is the seventh day and counts here and there; as above in seif 8; all the more permitted bathing and laundering; see below siman 426 — Magen Avraham end of siman sides regarding bathing one or two hours before dark and not before; in our case when seven are completed one may be lenient even before:
mishnah-berurah/19:_: (52) And the next day he tears — not literally; meaning motza'ei Shabbat. If he heard close report on Shabbat erev the festival, Shabbat counts for him one day and Yom Tov nullifies the seven-day decree [later authorities]; Pri Megadim Kaddish Yisrael wrote: the festival does not nullify and he has seven and thirty law even if he practiced one hour before the festival — see there:
beur-hagra/2:ב: If, etc. — there Tur wrote it counts:
beur-hagra/3:ב: Since, etc. — Hagahot Maimoniyot; as written 14:2 — but he does not practice his mourning on the festival if, etc., positive commandment, etc.; specifically on first Yom Tov and chol hamoed; but on last Yom Tov no positive commandment needed since it is rabbinic:
beur-hagra/14:_: (14) And reveals, etc. — and likewise — as written 14 regarding third week as Yoreh De'ah 399:12:
peri-megadim/1:_: This siman, etc. — Taz counts Yoreh De'ah 399 seven reasons; second Yom Tov is rabbinic and counts although we do not mourn on it at all; likewise per one view there, if one died and was buried on day one, nevertheless second Yom Tov counts — likewise for us it counts; and therefore there letter 8 and what Rabbenu Yerucham wrote here — second Yom Tov; I do not know a hint there except died and buried on second Yom Tov one does not mourn — one may say with difficulty; Peri Megadim here: second — lenient also on Rosh Hashanah even if buried on day one second Yom Tov counts for seven; explained further there:
peri-megadim/2:_: And days — Taz Yoreh De'ah 399 letter 2 expanded. For Levush: laundered garment in water alone on the festival — in custom of one hour before the festival, from thirty-day law one may say since custom forbids all thirty laundering; the one dealing publicly is permitted and may wear laundered in water alone, also laundered with carbonate — requires study siman 489:11 that we have no giyutz; siman 551:63; nevertheless in water alone, even if none other to wear, one may say permitted in such a case; I later saw this is an error, for it is explained seif 10 that in such a case permitted to launder and wear at night; therefore Yoreh De'ah 489 letters 2–3; nevertheless this has doubt whether our laundering is giyutz as below:
peri-megadim/5:ב: Ateret Zekenim wrote letter 7: if seven days passed from death one does not comfort the mourner afterward; likewise when erev Shabbat falls on last Yom Tov, even if seven days from death were not completed, one does not call "go out against the mourner" for it is public — Taz 427 beginning of siman. Requires study on close report: do they call "go out against the mourner" since seven days from death already passed? Perhaps all who did not know there is no comfort; specifically when he knew he already comforted himself that seven days passed — unlike this case. Regarding commerce: all who completed seven from death — permitted in private through servants or others in their houses, as siman 426; partner in shop — perhaps public forbidden; Or Sameach letter 6: I did not understand close report — although seven from death completed, commerce forbidden like other mourning; only on the festival where seven melacha days were nullified as we say; remaining matters explained in Magen Avraham:
biur-halacha/6:_: Within his house — see what Chacham Tzvi wrote; behold even though in Or Zarua it appears his practical conclusion is like his grandfather Maharash as we will quote below, Chacham Tzvi ruled like Ateret Zekenim because that colleague came later and mentioned only his view as we wrote in Mishna Berurah in his name; nevertheless what Chacham Tzvi was more lenient than him is not clear at all; I will quote Chacham Tzvi's words: a partner of a mourner who died on chol hamoed — permitted to deal in the shop immediately after Yom Tov [Ateret Zekenim siman 548] (what Ateret Zekenim concluded "like other mourning" means like there on the seventh day permitted to open his shop — so here if he died on the first day of chol hamoed permitted immediately after Yom Tov that is the seventh day) — it appears for us who practice prohibition only three days, likewise if he died on last Yom Tov — permitted — end quote; in truth not comparable, for there the mourner sat at least three days in mourning whereas here he has not sat at all; our leniency suffices if he died on chol hamoed on the first day per Ateret Zekenim, for at least now it is the seventh day from death — not to grasp two leniencies, three days and no mourning conduct at all [especially Pri Megadim doubts Ateret Zekenim too and tends to be stringent like his grandfather; if we are lenient like Ateret Zekenim, no more]. I quote Or Zarua: it appears to me a partner of a mourner who died on chol hamoed first day — permitted to deal in the shop immediately after Yom Tov, since we are lenient in other mourning after three days; but I heard in name of my grandfather the Gaon he ruled to forbid like other mourning — end quote; behold even Ateret Zekenim's view is only three days for a partner generally, as Maharshal; nevertheless in our case he was stringent specifically if died on chol hamoed first day so opening the shop is at least on the seventh day from death, as above; therefore the reason as we wrote above is clear in my humble opinion. Know that regarding close report it is simple: although seven days from death already passed, commerce is forbidden all mourning like other mourners, Yoreh De'ah 402 — close report is like burial day; so Pri Megadim end of siman:
biur-halacha/8:ג: Permitted to cut hair on erev Shabbat — likewise to launder and wash; it appears here one need not wait until after Mincha prayer, unlike above where it must be evident it is for festival honor — unlike here:
chokhmat-shlomo/1:_: Seif 1 — one who buries his dead during the festival, mourning does not apply on the festival, etc. NB: a case came before me where one became a mourner on Sukkot, may he read Torah on Simchat Torah? I permitted based on this: since everyone practices reading Torah, if the mourner does not read it is public; although one may distinguish — there Rabbenu Tam practiced reading in that place and it is public; but here perhaps he read elsewhere; R' Shlomo responsum 71 regarding a mourner who circumcised his son — he does not read Torah; nevertheless here another reason: since Shulchan Aruch permits a mourner on erev Yom Tov to leave for slichot, though other days forbidden — here since people increase slichot, pain if he sits home; likewise on Simchat Torah since all Israel read, pain if he sits and does not read; compare Taz Hilchot Shabbat 244 regarding attached melacha — marit ayin only when two sides to permit; if only one side to permit we fear perhaps this one knows it is not in the pot and will think he is a day laborer, etc.; so here. For one who circumcised his son there are two sides: perhaps they do not know today is milah day; if he has no milah he has no reason to read today; even if they know milah day perhaps he already read in another synagogue — therefore two sides to permit, no marit ayin concern. But on Simchat Torah since all read today and no other permit side except perhaps he read elsewhere — one may fear many know he did not read elsewhere and will recognize he refrains because of mourning — public. True one may distinguish Taz's case from ours; nevertheless at least no public concern, since rabbinic matter, especially on festival mourning does not apply; also from pain reason above one may be lenient — clear and correct for law; examine well:
kaf-hachayyim/2:_: (2) There — mourning does not apply on the festival, for they are days of joy and "you shall rejoice in your festival" — communal positive mitzvah overrides individual mourning positive mitzvah, even day one which is Torah positive mitzvah — Levush; all the more per view that no mourning is d'oraisa even day one, only aninut, as Beit Yosef in name of Rosh — see there; see Yoreh De'ah 399:13 that the world holds like those who say no mourning is d'oraisa — see there; see below seif 2:
kaf-hachayyim/5:_: (5) There — and counts thirty from burial day, etc.; Shulchan Aruch counts in place of seven and completes thirty as seif 16. R' Shlomo responsum 5, Mishna Berurah 71, Darkei Moshe Yoreh De'ah 399 letter 2; so Shach there s.k. 7. However in Hagahot Maimoniyot chapter 10 wrote: specifically when buried before Sukkot — Shmini Atzeret counts for seven as below seif 16; unlike here buried during festival — only one day counts — see there; Beit David, Beit Yosef Yoreh De'ah 399; so Shulchan Aruch there seif 2; Levush; Bach; Taz there s.k. 4 and this siman s.k. 4, wrote unlike R' Shlomo and Mishna Berurah who followed him — see there; so Magen Avraham s.k. 1; Or Sameach 13; letter 11 Hagahot Tashbetz; Beit David siman 314 wrote such should be practiced, do not say halacha follows the lenient here — see there; so in his book Yosef Ometz 93:2; Bigdei Yesha agreed with Taz — see there; Chayei Adam general rule 169:2, Mishna Berurah 4; nevertheless Chayei Adam wrote since some say Shmini Atzeret counts for seven one may be lenient where he suffers, etc., for bathing and women — see there; per Mordechai z"l Yoreh De'ah 481:1 in gloss they practice nowadays to forbid all bathing all thirty days; but by law otherwise permitted after seven — see there; if so where they did not practice per Mordechai, after seven bathing is permitted; see below letter 37:
kaf-hachayyim/17:_: (17) There — private matters apply; some say even private matters do not apply on the festival — Beit Yosef in name of Rambam; so Rashdam Chiddushei De'ot siman 202; Beit David Knesset HaGedolah in Hagahot Beit Yosef; but Shulchan Aruch ruled like most poskim that even on the festival private matters apply as Beit Yosef — see there; private matters are: shoes, bathing, Torah study as Yoreh De'ah siman 400 — see there; also some things called public — see there. Ateret Zekenim letter 3 to be lenient in Torah study on festival per view in Tur Yoreh De'ah 400 that study is public; although we do not rule so, nevertheless on festival one may rely on poskim who hold one does not practice even private matters — see there; so responsum Chacham Tzvi 100 to be lenient in study on festival — see there; Beit David Shaarei Teshuvah letter 5: if so obvious he may review Moed Katan chapter even if no obligation (as siman 285) — not worse than other study permitted — see there; nevertheless to read Torah on festival to count him among readers — l'chatchila not proper, Mishna Berurah 16:
levushei-serad/2:_: Magen Avraham s.k. 1 — as seif 16, meaning as seif 16: buried before festival — Shmini Atzeret counts seven days for thirty law; likewise buried on festival — although mourning begins after festival, Shmini Atzeret counts seven for thirty; so Shach Yoreh De'ah 399 s.k. 6; Hagahot Maimoniyot distinguishes — Shmini Atzeret does not count for seven unless buried before festival; so Taz Yoreh De'ah s.k. 4 and this siman s.k. 4:
levushei-serad/3:_: There — like inadvertent and did not practice. Law of inadvertent non-practice of mourning is this siman 66; his proof is unclear, for there Shulchan Aruch only wrote the festival does not nullify mourning and its law is like one who buries on the festival — see there; that is for everyone: even burying on festival Shmini Atzeret does not nullify mourning; whether Shmini Atzeret counts seven for thirty is unclear; it appears to Mishna Berurah and R' Shlomo that there too it counts seven since it wrote law like burying on festival — requires study:
levushei-serad/9:_: (s.k. 7) They do not wish. For it does not depend on willingness — whenever he can bury he is obligated to attend burial and aninut applies; therefore Shulchan Aruch wrote "and he does not wish" — meaning he has no ability; Shulchan Aruch afterward "and he wishes to bury" — meaning he has ability; question on Shulchan Aruch below also on second Yom Tov this language "and he wishes to bury" is redundant since permitted to bury, aninut applies even if some coercion prevents burial that day; so Mechaber Yoreh De'ah 341:1: on first Yom Tov if he wishes to bury through gentiles he practices aninut; on second Yom Tov it does not say "if he wishes" but since he himself may bury, aninut applies; see above 426:4; strained to say Shulchan Aruch here on second Yom Tov "if he wishes" comes to exclude total coercion such as corpse in captivity — as Yoreh De'ah 341; why teach these laws on Yom Tov since on weekday too the law is so — requires some study; know all Shulchan Aruch seif 7 is from Rosh Moed Katan as is, and there he did not write "if they wish to bury" only on first Yom Tov; on second Yom Tov he wrote anonymously aninut applies — see there:
levushei-serad/13:_: (Gloss seif 8) Bathing — for us. Explained Yoreh De'ah 481: for Mechaber bathing forbidden only seven days; Rama there: custom forbids all thirty:
rabbi-akiva-eiger/1:_: (Magen Avraham s.k. 5) placing tefillin on day one — see below siman 496 Magen Avraham s.k. 96; requires study:
shaarei-teshuvah/3:_: Second. Or Sameach; see responsum Bach Chadashot 9 who expanded to uphold this view that second day of Rosh Hashanah counts for him; likewise Diaspora second Yom Tov on Shabbat — even in Israel they could not practice mourning that day, nevertheless it counts and completes six for him; see Yoreh De'ah 399 in name of Bach and Beit Hillel there wrote so in Goren and responsum Torat Chayim:
shaarei-teshuvah/5:_: In private — Or Sameach; it implies from Magen Avraham that even Torah study is permitted only for bad matters; Chacham Tzvi 100 wrote he ruled for a scholar accustomed to review Mishnayot by heart — permitted to review all the festival, even though private matters apply; nevertheless permitted: one, no greater loss than forgetting if he does not review; we do not find permission for loss except in what is not actual joy; further, specifically other years when he could engage in Jeremiah, etc.; on festival improper to engage in this and improper to sit idle from Torah; also Rambam holds on festival one does not practice even private matters; see Yoreh De'ah 399 Tur and Beit Yosef — Rambam is not alone; therefore even without loss in memorized Mishnayot one may rely on Rambam and supporters to learn "all the ordinances of the Holy One, blessed be He, are upright," etc. — see there; if so obvious he may review Moed Katan chapter even without obligation — not worse than other permitted study — see there:
shaarei-teshuvah/13:_: Prohibition. Or Sameach; see below end siman 426 and Magen Avraham there; see responsum Teshuvat Chen 31 wondered on Shach Yoreh De'ah 481 that immersion of the whole body in cold water has no prohibition per the lenient view — see there; although somewhat appears so from Rama's plain wording, one may reject; so they practiced to be lenient in cold immersion as Shach's words:
